ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law 10/2010 of 28 April on the prevention of money laundering and terrorist financing (as amended); Royal Decree 304/2014 of 5 May approving the regulation for the implementation of Law 10/2010 on beneficial ownership information

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, and shareholders against OFAC SDN list, UN sanctions, EU sanctions, and Spanish AML authorities per Law 10/2010; PEP identification and enhanced due diligence required

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Strict adherence to Spanish language and Latin script; no foreign language or transliteration permitted
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Terms reserved for public administration or semi-public entities (e.g., 'Banco', 'Caja de Ahorros', 'Estado', 'Gobierno') without prior approval
Names identical or confusing with existing registered companies
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If name is rejected, submit administrative appeal to the competent Registrar within one month; further appeal possible to the Ministry of Justice or courts

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Accepted for SL companies provided a registered office address is maintained for service of process and to fulfill commercial substance requirements; virtual offices are widely used in logistics and e-commerce sectors
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low risk (typically under 5-10% for routine SL formations without indications of fraud or non-compliance)

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ley 1/2010, de 5 de marzo, de Sociedades de Responsabilidad Limitada (LSRL), Articles 1-100
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Escritura Pública de Constitución y Estatutos Sociales
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum subscribed and paid-up capital of 3,000 EUR; full payment required upon incorporation with no escrow account mandated for standard SL formation
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: The Board of Directors of the proposed [Company Name] Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada, convened on [Date], unanimously resolved to: (i) approve the full subscription of the minimum share capital of three thousand euros by the incorporators; (ii) establish the registered office at [full address], Barcelona, Spain; (iii) appoint [Name] as Managing Director and [Name] as Corporate Secretary; and (iv) authorize the preparation and filing of the incorporation public deed with the competent Registro Mercantil authorities, along with all related statutory and tax filings. This resolution is binding and shall take immediate effect. (Word count: 98)

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft and Sign Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the estatutos sociales in Spanish detailing share capital, corporate object, administration, and governance. Have all incorporators sign before a notary public.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Amendments permitted within 30 days if notary identifies deficiencies

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit signed public deed and estatutos to notary for execution. Pay notarization and registration fees.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Request supplementary documentation if application is queried

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the notarized public deed online or in person at the provincial Registro Mercantil. Obtain registration certificate and NIF application.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Appeal to Mercantile Court within statutory period if rejected

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Fiscal Identification (NIF) and Final Registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit registration certificate to AEAT for NIF issuance and complete any required tax registrations.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Follow-up submission if processing delay occurs

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Local Ayuntamiento and Registro Mercantil for mercantile authorization

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry for the Ecological Transition and Demographic Challenge
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No specific discharge or emissions thresholds applicable; standard waste management and air quality regulations apply

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification from local fire department, structural load inspections, and workplace safety clearance from labor authorities

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT), Ministerio de Hacienda; e-Office: Sede Electrónica de la AEAT (sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es); customs matters: Departamento de Aduanas e Impuestos Especiales.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada (SL): (1) execute the public incorporation deed before a notary, who obtains the provisional NIF (CIF) from AEAT at the time of signing; (2) inscribe the SL in the Registro Mercantil within two months of the deed; (3) after registration, submit Form 036 (censo de empresarios) together with the registry certificate to obtain the definitive NIF; (4) the definitive NIF serves as the VAT identification number (format ES+NIF); (5) activate electronic channels by obtaining a digital certificate (FNMT or PSC) and enrolling in the AEAT electronic office; (6) a non-resident entity without a permanent establishment must appoint a Spanish tax representative and obtain an NIF-N via Form 036; non-established EU suppliers may register directly at the AEAT e-Office.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation — an SL is a standalone taxpayer subject to Corporate Income Tax (Impuesto sobre Sociedades, LIS) on worldwide income at 25% (with reduced rates available for new small companies in their first years); pass-through status is not available in Spain.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box classification exists; entity status is statutory under the Ley de Sociedades de Capital and LIS. Available elections: (i) corporate income tax group consolidation (Art. 63 LIS) for groups with at least 70% ownership; (ii) VAT group regime (Art. 163 decies LIVA) for closely controlled entities; (iii) ETVE (Spanish international holding company) special regime for participation and dividend exemption; (iv) OSS (Union and non-Union) and IOSS schemes for distance sales and low-value import consignments; (v) hybrid mismatch rules under ATAD transposition (Arts. 15 bis-15 quinquies LIS) are mandatory with no opt-out.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax — IVA (Impuesto sobre el Valor Añadido), governed by Ley 37/1992 (LIVA) and RD 1624/1992 (Reglamento).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general VAT registration threshold for established taxpayers — registration is compulsory from the first taxable supply in Spain. For non-established EU distance sellers the intra-EU distance sales threshold is EUR 10,000 (below which VAT follows the Member State of dispatch and the OSS regime may be used); non-EU suppliers are registrable without threshold from the first transaction.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Real-time VAT records filing under SII (Suministro Inmediato de Información): mandatory for taxpayers with turnover above EUR 6,000,000 and for VAT groups on all issued and received invoices; records must be transmitted to AEAT through authenticated web services (API) in XML schema with digital signature/certificate within 4 calendar days from the date of accrual; no fiscal stamping is used. E-invoice interoperability: Law 18/2022 (Crea y Crece) and RD 1007/2023 (Verifactu) require certified billing software ensuring invoice integrity, traceability, immediate accessibility to AEAT and a verifiable QR code; the B2B e-invoicing issuance mandate between entrepreneurs will become effective upon publication of the implementing ministerial order (expected during 2025-2026).

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods physically exported by the cross-dock/3PL operator or by its foreign principal from Spanish customs territory to a third country are exempt with credit (0%) under Art. 21 LIVA, provided the operator holds the customs export declaration and proves the goods left the EU within 90 days of dispatch. Export-related services (transport, loading, handling, warehousing and related processing incident to an export) are zero-rated under Art. 22.3 LIVA. B2B cross-dock fulfilment and warehousing services supplied to a non-established business customer are placed outside Spanish VAT under Art. 70.1.5 LIVA (taxable at the customer's jurisdiction), allowing zero-tax invoicing with reverse charge abroad; the exemption fails where documentation does not substantiate the customer's foreign establishment or the actual exit of the goods. Goods under customs warehousing or temporary admission remain VAT-suspended until definitive export.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (DUA - Documento Único Administrativo / SAD) with item-level HS codes, weights and values
Bill of Lading, Air Waybill or CMR consigned to the overseas principal or its agent evidencing physical departure from EU territory
Inward Remittance Certificate - bank SWIFT MT103 or credit advice evidencing collection of export proceeds into a Spanish bank account
Commercial invoice and packing list reconciled with the DUA declared values
Transport contract or booking confirmation showing the INCOTERMS applicable and the port/airport/land border of exit
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: AEAT conducts post-clearance export verification; the taxpayer must produce the DUA, transport and payment evidence within 30 days of an official request. Wrongful application of the export exemption results in: (i) retroactive VAT assessment on the invoiced amount plus statutory late-payment interest (interés de demora) from the date of invoicing; (ii) an administrative penalty of 50% to 150% of the understated tax under Art. 193 LGT; (iii) invoicing infringement penalties under Art. 201 LGT of EUR 300 to EUR 3,000; (iv) referral to criminal jurisdiction for VAT fraud under Art. 305 of the Código Penal where the undue amount exceeds EUR 120,000 in one financial year (term of imprisonment 2-6 years); AEAT claims expire after the 4-year prescription period from the accrual date.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de España (Bank of Spain) as the central bank and executing agent for monetary and external statistics; the competent regulatory body for foreign transactions is the Dirección General de Transacciones Internacionales (DGTI) of the Spanish Ministry of Economy under the framework of Law 19/2003 and Royal Decree 1815/1991.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Spain enjoys full capital and current account convertibility inside the EU passport area under Articles 63-65 TFEU and Spanish Law 19/2003. The euro is freely convertible; no prior administrative authorization is required for capital injections, profit distribution to non-resident shareholders, trade payments, or repatriation of liquidation proceeds. The residual practical constraints are limited to statistical declaration thresholds, AML/CFT due diligence, validation of the underlying transaction purpose, and anti-terrorist financing controls on counterparties resident in high-risk third countries, particularly LatAm routes. Profit remittance via dividend or shareholder loan service is permitted without withholding obstacles beyond the standard corporate income tax and possible non-resident withholding tax formalities under the Spain-Latam tax treaties.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Spain imposes no statutory surrender of export proceeds to the central bank or any mandatory conversion ratio. Export collections may remain in foreign currency accounts and may be freely held, converted into euros, or used for inbound/outbound trade. Nevertheless, all export transactions must be reported for statistical monitoring through the Declaración de Transacciones de Pagos Exteriores (DTPE) when the operation equals or exceeds €10,000, with monthly aggregation under Ministerial Order EHA/3039/2005 and Royal Decree 1815/1991; the reporting is fulfilled by the resident account-holding bank for receipts routed through Spanish accounts.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (Managing Current Account, EUR and multi-currency)
Operational Account + FX Hedging and Trade Finance Facility
Operational Account + Escrow/Deposit Account for 3PL collections
Operational Account for commerce and supply-chain settlements

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: High viability as a secondary clearing engine: EU-licensed Electronic Money Institutions (EMIs) such as Airwallex and Wise Europe can passport into Spain under PSD2 to provide IBAN-denominated euro accounts, multi-currency virtual accounts, cross-border wires, and local ACH/SEPA disbursements. Legal constraints are (i) EMIs are not credit institutions and may not grant overdraft or deposit guarantees, (ii) the SL must retain a primary treasury relationship with a full-reserve Spanish bank to access capital escrow, trade finance, or large-volume FX lines, and (iii) the EMI must be supervised by the Bank of Spain or its home-state regulator with proper intensified due diligence on LatAm counterparties. Thus, an EMI is appropriate for clearing ancillary merchant settlements and vendor payouts, not for the core statutory treasury mandate.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Spanish AML Law 10/2010 and Royal Decree 304/2014 require identification of the legal entity and its real owners, confirmation of the mandate of the representatives, and execution of the KYC interview. For the SL, at least one director or an authorized signatory with an NIE (Número de Identificación de Extranjero) and physical presence in Spain is strongly preferred by tier-1 banks; fully remote opening now exists under the CNMV/Banker's Association’s video-identification protocol, but only when the corporate documents are notarized, apostilled, and accompanied by original UBO certification. For a cross-border 3PL serving LatAm, most Spanish banks will demand either (i) an in-person appointment in a Spanish branch to verify the CEO or UBO, or (ii) a video-identification process with notarial appointment, digital signature, and enhanced documentary review. Foreign non-bank signatories cannot open an account solely with a Powers of Attorney; the AP must be granted before a notary and registered with the Commercial Registry.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk or monitored LatAm jurisdiction flags (Mexico, Brazil, Colombia, Peru) on counterparties and fund routes.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized and apostilled Registry Mercantil excerpt of the SL, up-to-date UBO declaration (Registro de Titularidades Reales), audited or bank-certified financial statements, signed commercial warehouse and fulfilment agreements, customer purchase orders and invoice register, customs AR/EX/SAD files, and an economic substance memorandum evidencing Spanish personnel, inventory control, and pricing discipline.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear source-of-funds or circularity for inbound capital injection from the LatAm parent or shareholder.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Public deed of capital increase or shareholder loan instrument, shareholder funds provenance proof (tax returns, audited statements of the shareholder, dividend declarations, sale of assets contracts), bank reference letters from the remitting institution, SWIFT MT103 with exact purpose code, and confirmation that the SL has filed the relevant DGTI notification via the bank if required.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Mismatch between ISIC 5210 / 3PL activity and the payment pattern generating atypical trade-based money-laundering red flags.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete transaction chain: e-commerce order data, warehouse inbound/outbound manifests, transport waybills (CMR, airway bill, ocean B/L), customs clearance documents, supplier/vendor invoices, and commercial contracts with the overseas warehouse operator; develop a standardized payment file with unique SFTP/invoice hashes that match bank wire narratives.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity or subordinated shareholder loans from the non-resident parent into the Spanish SL must be executed by SWIFT MT103 from the remitting bank to the SL's Spanish euro account. The bank reference field must contain the correct Spanish external transaction concept code (for capital: ‘Inversiones directas / Ampliación de capital’ – DTPE group 3.1.1; for shareholder loans: group 3.1.9 or 8.1.1 depending on classification) and the unique corporate identifier (NIF/CIF and register book entry). The capital increase itself must be formalized in a notarial deed deposited in the Mercantile Registry; the SL must issue the certificate of capital subscription and submit the bank's credit advice to the registry as part of the filing. Spanish banks perform post-credit verification by requiring the deed, a certificate of UBO, and the shareholder register extract; the bank will automatically report all volumetric foreign transactions via DTPE, while the SL must keep in its defence file the stamping certificate of the deed, the NIE of the shareholder, and evidence of the operative Falcondo economic-substance nexus for the 3PL.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For 3PL vendor payments (warehouse leases, last-mile carriers, fulfilment technology fees) and trade settlements, the preferred rails are: (1) SWIFT MT103 via the corporate internet banking channel for international wires to non-EU vendors, including LatAm, with correct UETR and purpose code selected (ISO 20022 'TRADE' or specific 'PURP' depending on the nature); (2) Commercial Irrevocable Letters of Credit (at sight or deferred) issued by the Spanish bank in favour of overseas warehouse operators for recurring standby season, with full compliance under UCP600; (3) SEPA Instant Credit (SCT Inst) for EU-based logistics partners in euro; and (4) Local ACH rails in USD via correspondents for LatAm branches when the bank's FX desk provides a locked conversion. Each disbursement must be invoice-backed and retained in the payment compliance folder to ensure the bank's transfer-pricing and KYC audit obligations are satisfied.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: EUR/MXN FX spot and deliverable forwards with a licensed Spanish credit institution or EU-authorized broker, backed by a real underlying trade transaction
EUR/BRL and EUR/CLP Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) with authorized counterparties when sovereign currency restrictions or illiquid deliverable markets impede physical delivery
Cross-currency swaps (EUR/USD/COP or EUR/USD/MXN) under ISDA 2002 or Spanish ANI? framework, used only for hedging forecast 3PL revenue and cost flows arising from the overseas warehouse operations
At-market FX options (call/put on EUR versus LatAm currencies) for contingent cash-flow exposure of high-volatility routes, provided the option does not create speculative leverage

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Spanish Tax Agency (Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria, AEAT)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 25 calendar days following the six-month period after the end of the tax year; for a calendar-year company, generally 1 to 25 July of the following year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing may trigger a surcharge generally ranging from 1% plus 1% per completed month of delay to 15% after twelve months, plus late-payment interest where applicable; concealed tax deficiencies may incur penalties of 50% to 150% of the unpaid tax.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Approval of annual accounts and management report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders' meeting of the Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual accounts must be approved within six months after the end of the financial year; for a calendar-year company, generally by 30 June.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to approve accounts prevents timely statutory filing and may contribute to Mercantile Registry closure and director liability exposure; no separate filing fee applies to the shareholders' approval itself.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Deposit of annual accounts, management report, and auditor's report where applicable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after approval of the annual accounts; for accounts approved on 30 June, generally by 30 July.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines generally range from approximately EUR 1,200 to EUR 60,000, subject to statutory calculation rules; higher limits may apply to larger companies. After one year from the filing deadline, the Registry may close the company's registration, restricting further filings except permitted exceptions.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual beneficial ownership identification statement filed with the annual accounts
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Competent Spanish Mercantile Registry and the Central Register of Beneficial Ownership, as applicable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filed with the annual accounts and updated whenever beneficial ownership information changes; additional registry or electronic reporting requirements may apply under current Central Register procedures.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Incorrect, incomplete, or outdated beneficial ownership information may result in registry filing deficiencies, registration restrictions, and administrative or anti-money-laundering sanctions.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation and maintenance of the Register of Members
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Company records; relevant changes may be reflected in notarial instruments and the Mercantile Registry where legally required
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No separate annual return is required solely for the Register of Members; update promptly after each transfer, encumbrance, or other change and verify the register during the annual accounts cycle.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to maintain accurate ownership records may impair enforcement of shareholder rights, create evidentiary and director-liability risks, and cause deficiencies in related beneficial ownership filings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual related-party and related-transaction information return (Modelo 232), if applicable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Generally during the month following the ten-month period after the end of the tax year; for a calendar-year company, generally 1 to 30 November. Filing is conditional on statutory related-party transaction thresholds or qualifying transactions.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or inaccurate filing may result in tax information-reporting penalties and increased transfer-pricing audit exposure.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Independent statutory audit is generally mandatory where, for two consecutive financial years, the company exceeds at least two of these thresholds: total assets of EUR 2.85 million, annual net turnover of EUR 5.7 million, or average employees of 50. Audit is also mandatory in specified regulated, public-interest, group, or other statutory cases.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Spanish General Accounting Plan (Plan General de Contabilidad, Spanish GAAP). IFRS is mandatory for certain consolidated listed-group accounts and may apply in other legally permitted circumstances; it is not the default framework for an ordinary Spanish SL's individual accounts.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The company must identify and maintain current information on its ultimate beneficial owners, generally the individuals ultimately owning or controlling more than 25% or otherwise exercising control. Beneficial ownership information is confirmed through the annual accounts filing and updated upon any change. Share transfers must be documented and entered in the Register of Members; they are not generally subject to a separate annual share-transfer return.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Contracts between the company and its sole shareholder, where applicable

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: EUR 600-1,800 per year for registered-office, corporate-secretarial, and filing-agent services; Spain does not generally impose a separate annual registered-agent renewal fee.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: EUR 1,500-8,000 for a non-complex statutory audit of an SL; fees increase with turnover, inventory, cross-border transactions, group reporting, and regulated activities.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Reduced rates: 15% for newly created SLs carrying out an economic activity in the first two taxable periods with a positive tax base (art. 29.1 Ley 27/2014 LIS), subject to a EUR 300,000 taxable-base cap per period; 20% for cooperatives. Incentive credits: R&D and innovation tax credits (25%-50% of qualifying expenditures), job-creation credits, environmental investment credits, patent box regime exempting 60% of qualified IP-sourced income, and participation exemption for dividends from qualifying non-resident subsidiaries. Spanish tax losses (bases imponibles negativas) benefit from indefinite carryforward under general law, with quantitative caps: offset limited to 70% of the positive tax base for entities with net turnover below EUR 20 million, 60% for turnover between EUR 20 million and EUR 60 million, and 25% or 50% for large taxpayers, with a residual EUR 1 million floor always available for offset.
